THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:8068  CRL.P No. 101068 of 2022  ORDER 1.

This petition has been filed challenging the registration of the FIR which has culminated in filing of a charge sheet against the petitioner, who is accused No.2.
2.

The allegation against the petitioner is that he had collected certain sums of money from the complainant in order to secure his two sons jobs in Unaided Colleges and on them being recruited,
their posts would be admitted to grant.

3. The petitioner is placing reliance on certain documents, which relate to withdrawal of the monies from the accounts of the complainant's bank and the amount stated to have been deposited in the accounts of the other accused.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that it is purely cheque bounce case, the defacto-complainant instead of prosecuting the petitioner under Section 138 of the N.I. Act, he has filed false case under Section 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code (for short, 'the IPC').
5.

From perusal of the charge sheet and materials available on record, accused No.2 is disputing the question of fact that cannot be gone into under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C, NC: 2024:KHC-D:8068 the similar view was taken by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.
Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and others1.
6.

sentences.text: From perusal of the FIR and charge sheet materials, the prima facie case is made out so as to attract sections 406 and 420 of the IPC.
The complaint and charge sheet prima facie discloses the cognizable offence.

7. It is no more Res integra that excess of powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C to quash a criminal proceedings is only when an allegation made in the FIR and charge sheet constitutes the ingredients of the offence alleged.
Interference by this Court under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C to prevent the abuse of process of law in the Court or otherwise secure the ends of justice.

8. It is settled law that any documents or defence statement produced by the accused for his defence cannot be looked into by Court, except in very exceptional circumstances, at the initial stage of the criminal proceedings.

It is trite law that, this Court cannot embark upon the appreciation in the AIR 2021 SC 1918 NC: 2024:KHC-D:8068 evidence while considering the petition filed under Section Mallikarjun Gowda S/O Basanagowda vs State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27903810/
2 482 of the Cr.P.C for quashing criminal proceedings.

It is clear from the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, if a prima facie case is made out disclosing the ingredients of the offence alleged against the accused Court cannot quash the criminal proceedings.

9. In my view, having regard to the materials on the basis of which the charge sheet has been filed,
this is not a fit case to invoke Section 482 of the Cr.P.C to quash the proceedings as a matter requires a trial.
In similar circumstance the Coordinate Bench of this Court dismissed the petition filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. in Criminal Petition No.101156/2022.
Hence, petition is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, the criminal petition is dismissed.
10. Hence, the trial Court shall make an endeavor to expedite the trial.

11. Any observations made in this petition, do not come in the way of trial Court while deciding the matter and the trial Court is at liberty to dispose of the matter in accordance with law, expeditiously without influenced by the order passed by this Court.
In view of disposal of the petition, pending interlocutory applications do not survive for consideration and accordingly, same are dismissed.
